body:
## Summary
Implements comprehensive autonomous behavior system for proactive agent actions, completing story LIN-59 (5 points) of the Linear Agent Interactive Capabilities epic.

- ✅ Core autonomous behavior engine with plugin architecture
- ✅ 6 production-ready behaviors (story monitoring, ART health, dependency detection, workflow automation, periodic reporting, anomaly detection)
- ✅ Integration with webhook system from LIN-57
- ✅ Comprehensive test coverage

## Implementation Details

### Core Architecture
- **AutonomousBehaviorEngine**: Orchestrates behavior registration, triggering, and execution with rate limiting
- **BehaviorScheduler**: Manages periodic behavior execution using cron-like scheduling
- **HealthMonitor**: Tracks behavior performance metrics and health status
- **BehaviorRegistry**: Central management for all behaviors with configuration support

### Implemented Behaviors
1. **Story Monitoring** (Priority 80)
   - Monitors stories >5 points and suggests decomposition
   - Posts actionable suggestions with example breakdowns

2. **ART Health Monitoring** (Priority 90)
   - Monitors ART readiness using SAFe modules
   - Alerts when readiness drops below 85%
   - Generates detailed health reports

3. **Dependency Detection** (Priority 70)
   - Analyzes issue content for potential dependencies
   - Detects circular dependencies
   - Suggests relationship types with confidence scores

4. **Workflow Automation** (Priority 60)
   - Automates label management based on state transitions
   - Handles blocked state notifications
   - Synchronizes parent-child issue states
   - Detects and marks stale issues

5. **Periodic Reporting** (Priority 40)
   - Generates scheduled reports (weekly, sprint, velocity)
   - Calculates team metrics and trends
   - Provides actionable insights

6. **Anomaly Detection** (Priority 50)
   - Detects 8 types of anomalies in team performance
   - Compares against historical baselines
   - Takes corrective actions for critical issues

### Integration Points
- Webhook events trigger behaviors via `webhook-integration.ts`
- Scheduled triggers for periodic behaviors
- Manual triggers for testing/admin
- Command completion triggers for follow-up actions

## Test Coverage
- Individual behavior unit tests
- Integration tests for behavior interactions
- Webhook processing tests
- Error handling and recovery tests

## Future Enhancements
- AI-powered behavior suggestions (deferred to future work)
- Custom behavior plugin system
- Advanced anomaly detection algorithms
- Real-time notification channels

## Breaking Changes
None - all changes are additive

## Dependencies
- Linear SDK
- Existing webhook infrastructure (LIN-57)
- SAFe modules for ART planning

## Related Issues
- Closes #146
- Part of Epic LIN-56
- Depends on LIN-57, LIN-58

- [x] Code follows project conventions
- [x] Tests pass locally
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] No security vulnerabilities introduced
- [x] Linear issue will be updated to Done after merge

author: cwille97
body:
This PR adds support for OpenAI models hosted on [Azure AI Foundry](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/ai-foundry). I tested manually using my own GPT-4.1 endpoint hosted in Azure AI Foundry. `AsyncAzureOpenAI` is required to make requests to Azure as documented [here](https://github.com/openai/openai-python?tab=readme-ov-file#microsoft-azure-openai). This PR introduces the following parameters which are unique to models hosted on Azure:
* `azure_deployment` this is the deployment name which you enter when creating the resources
* `api_version` this will differ based on the model and can be found in the Azure portal when viewing the details of your deployment. 

`base_url` corresponds to the "Target URI" in Azure, but you can drop the url parameters as those will be provided using the variables mentioned above. The `api_key` is copied from the "Key" field.

body:
## Summary
- Fixes the "Failed to initialize Gemini model: Error: Error creating contentGenerator: Unsupported authType: undefined" error
- Changes authType from 'api-key' to 'gemini-api-key' for API key authentication

## Root Cause
The ai-sdk-provider-gemini-cli package's initializeGeminiClient function only recognizes these authType values:
- 'gemini-api-key' → maps to AuthType.USE_GEMINI
- 'oauth-personal' → maps to AuthType.LOGIN_WITH_GOOGLE_PERSONAL  
- 'vertex-ai' → maps to AuthType.USE_VERTEX_AI

Our implementation was using 'api-key' which didn't match any condition, causing authType to become undefined and triggering the error.

body:
## Summary by Sourcery

Enable robust streaming JSON parsing by removing fixed escape reservations, adding buffer compaction support in StreamBuffer and StreamParser, refactoring position tracking APIs, and bolstering tests for low-memory and stress scenarios

New Features:
- Add StreamBuffer::compact_from method to slide unprocessed data and free buffer space
- Implement From<&str> conversion for JSON string wrapper

Enhancements:
- Remove static escape_reserve and allow full-buffer unescaped byte appends
- Refactor StreamParser to trigger buffer compaction on overflow and update parser state positions
- Simplify ContentRange API to track content_start for strings, keys, and numbers
- Adjust parsing logic to refill only when buffer is empty and integrate compaction for continuous streaming

Tests:
- Add comprehensive tests for buffer compaction behavior and edge cases
- Introduce stress tests for minimal buffer sizes, escape sequences, and varied read chunk scenarios

author: horner
body:
## Summary

This commit adds exponential temperature prediction for cooking time estimation, using a physics-based model that considers grill temperature and heat transfer.

https://xkcd.com/612/
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gTLDuxmQek

## Changes Made

### 🔄 Modified Files

#### `cmd/root.go`
- Integrated exponential predictor with historical data loading
- Loads recent data on startup for ETA stability
- Uses exponential model with linear fallback
- Added debug logging for model state and prediction sources

#### `graph.go`
- Added probe ETA plotting capability
- Shows predicted time-to-completion on temperature charts
- ETA values scaled to fit within temperature range
- Only displays when ETA data is available

#### `update.go`
- Added JSONDuration type for time.Duration serialization
- Added ProbeETA field to Status struct
- Proper marshaling/unmarshaling of duration values

## Technical Details

### Physics-Based Modeling
- Exponential approach: `T(t) = T_equilibrium - (T_equilibrium - T_start) × e^(-t/τ)`
- Time constant (tau) estimated from cooking data
- Considers grill temperature effects on meat heating

### Prediction Logic
- Calculates effective equilibrium temperature based on grill conditions
- Accounts for grill temperature consistency
- Multi-factor analysis including temperature differential and cooking stage
- Linear prediction fallback when exponential model isn't suitable

### Data Handling
- Uses recent data for initialization
- Time constant updates with new measurements
- Least squares fitting for tau estimation
- Tracks prediction uncertainty

## Benefits

- Physics-based predictions instead of linear extrapolation
- Better initial estimates using historical data
- Accounts for grill limitations and cooking physics
- ETA trends visible on temperature graphs
- Forecast command for testing model performance
- Tunable parameters for different cooking styles
- Debug logging for model visibility

## Testing

The forecast command validates model performance against historical cooking data:

```bash
./wifire forecast --input cook.json --actual 2025-07-05T20:49:45-04:00
```

Sample output:
```
Time       Probe    Target   Exp ETA      Actual       Accuracy  
19:31:34   190      204      1h17m        1h18m        -0.6%     
19:35:42   194      204      1h12m        1h14m        -1.8%     
19:41:15   198      204      1h08m        1h08m        +0.1%     
```

## Configuration

Parameters are documented in `prediction.md` and can be tuned for different cooking styles:

```go
// Default settings
minDataPoints: 3
timeConstant: 3600.0  // 1 hour
tauRange: 300s - 28800s (5min - 8hr)

// Fast grilling example
minDataPoints: 2
tauRange: 180s - 7200s (3min - 2hr)
```

## Notes

- Existing functionality unchanged
- New features are additive
- Forecast command is separate tool
- ETA field optional in JSON output
- Linear fallback preserves original behavior

body:
This pull request introduces a series of changes across multiple files to enhance functionality, improve code clarity, and ensure consistency in parameter usage. The most significant updates involve the addition of default agent handling for various functions, the implementation of real-time ASR capabilities, and adjustments to logging levels and formats.

### Enhancements to ASR and Real-time Streaming:

* **`examples/asr-agent/client.py`**: Added a WebSocket-based client implementation for real-time audio streaming, including audio recording with `pyaudio` and sending data to an ASR server. The client handles connection events and processes server responses.
* **`examples/asr-agent/realtime-agent.py`**: Implemented a real-time ASR agent with stream handling capabilities, integration with chat tools, and notification handling. The agent processes audio data and generates responses using the `gpt-4o` model.

### Refactoring for Default Agent Handling:

* **`sdk/python/spear/utils/io.py`**: Updated functions like `input`, `speak`, and `record` to use a default global agent (`client.global_agent()`) if no agent is explicitly provided. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4e5c79f25abcc4865b4033bf43e351a0258228502d864fe388a6e8e07f9ebce3L14-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4e5c79f25abcc4865b4033bf43e351a0258228502d864fe388a6e8e07f9ebce3L36-R43) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4e5c79f25abcc4865b4033bf43e351a0258228502d864fe388a6e8e07f9ebce3L76-R81)
* **`sdk/python/spear/utils/tool.py`**: Modified `register_internal_tool` to support default agent handling, improving usability and reducing boilerplate code.
* **Various test files (`misc/OPEA`, `sdk/python/tests`, `workload/docker/python`)**: Adjusted calls to `chat.chat`, `io.input`, and other functions to use the updated agent parameter format. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4a8b1b68f8b5138b15f9813cabb4d290d2a4c0948ffccdd42b0185fd6d9f2dc1L54-R54) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4a8b1b68f8b5138b15f9813cabb4d290d2a4c0948ffccdd42b0185fd6d9f2dc1L79) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-409ab1bf5f3edad390dad8bcdebec27bafeda004033a672c3f827ba756ed095eL37-R37)

### Logging Improvements:

* **`sdk/python/spear/transform/chat.py`**: Changed logging level from `DEBUG` to `INFO` for better alignment with production-level logging practices.
* **`examples/asr-agent/client.py` and `examples/asr-agent/realtime-agent.py`**: Added detailed logging to track connection events, errors, and data processing steps. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4dfec7704653d5471cdc927ea0373664f019b4f3b3f0e871bd40ccdd338679b8R1-R83) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-946cc5e57cbbeb0c7479c7c56ad35dbbc74ec6f36eaafa3ea801a3a0432c168bR1-R162)

author: ayazs
body:
This PR contributes a new application to the community_contributions section: a personal assistant chatbot enhanced with real-time weather awareness using the Open-Meteo API. The assistant can now respond naturally to weather-related topics in conversation, while continuing to represent the individual whose profile is provided in the me/ folder.

**Key features:**
- Integrates Open-Meteo APIs for real-time weather data and geocoding
- Adds a get_weather tool callable by the assistant via function calling
- Enhances conversation with natural weather references (e.g. current, user-mentioned, or hypothetical locations)
- Preserves original assistant behaviour and purpose (personal branding, question tracking)
- Includes updated README.md with setup instructions, example prompts, and attribution

**To run:**
- Update your .env file with `BOT_SELF_NAME` set to the name the assistant uses to refer to itself (e.g. "Ed", "Alex", etc.)
- Populate the me/ directory with your linkedin.pdf and summary.txt
- Install dependencies (`uv add openmeteo_requests`)
- Launch via `uv run app.py`

body:
I'd like to `brew install buildkite/buildkite/buildkite-mcp-server`. Goreleaser [supports homebrew casks](https://goreleaser.com/customization/homebrew_casks/), and we have [a homebrew tap](https://github.com/buildkite/homebrew-buildkite), so let's switch it on!

On this branch, I ran:

```console
$ goreleaser release --snapshot
```

This generates casks like:

```ruby
# This file was generated by GoReleaser. DO NOT EDIT.
cask "buildkite-mcp-server" do
  desc "Model Context Protocol server for Buildkite"
  homepage "https://github.com/buildkite/buildkite-mcp-server"
  version "0.5.5-SNAPSHOT-51c2883"

  livecheck do
    skip "Auto-generated on release."
  end

  binary "buildkite-mcp-server"

  on_macos do
    on_intel do
      url "https://github.com/buildkite/buildkite-mcp-server/releases/download/v0.5.5/buildkite-mcp-server_Darwin_x86_64.tar.gz"
      sha256 "d380dcda54d4217be8a4004bd2fa0777ea772d0235e72580a3f5c7dea7f167df"
    end
    on_arm do
      url "https://github.com/buildkite/buildkite-mcp-server/releases/download/v0.5.5/buildkite-mcp-server_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz"
      sha256 "5ef3a3a38d11d85ae76ad0d896c6436605248503c5c2842b3abdd0740ddbd0ee"
    end
  end

  on_linux do
    on_intel do
      url "https://github.com/buildkite/buildkite-mcp-server/releases/download/v0.5.5/buildkite-mcp-server_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz"
      sha256 "1905a1c1accb1c508b25ad3da815ed03e5b2ce353d00dfc98c9a3cf288a52ce0"
    end
    on_arm do
      url "https://github.com/buildkite/buildkite-mcp-server/releases/download/v0.5.5/buildkite-mcp-server_Linux_arm64.tar.gz"
      sha256 "e7c43a14957501a136720066462d3224cdfa6089c0bb929915148307047d8f26"
    end
  end

  postflight do
    if system_command("/usr/bin/xattr", args: ["-h"]).exit_status == 0
      system_command "/usr/bin/xattr", args: ["-dr", "com.apple.quarantine", "#{staged_path}/buildkite-mcp-server"]
    end
  end

  # No zap stanza required
end
```

I copy pasted this into my local clone of the tap, adjusted it to [the latest official v0.5.5 artifacts](https://github.com/buildkite/buildkite-mcp-server/releases/tag/v0.5.5), and it works a treat:

```console
$ brew install buildkite/buildkite/buildkite-mcp-server
==> Auto-updating Homebrew...
Adjust how often this is run with HOMEBREW_AUTO_UPDATE_SECS or disable with
HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE. Hide these hints with HOMEBREW_NO_ENV_HINTS (see `man brew`).
==> Downloading https://github.com/buildkite/buildkite-mcp-server/releases/download/v0.5.5/buildkite-mcp-server_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz
Already downloaded: /Users/sj26/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads/e4ea39ee1b140052feff876f6ae31313b6296b54301e6ee57f615cf850469731--buildkite-mcp-server_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz
==> Installing Cask buildkite-mcp-server
==> Linking Binary 'buildkite-mcp-server' to '/opt/homebrew/bin/buildkite-mcp-server'
🍺  buildkite-mcp-server was successfully installed!
```
```console
$ buildkite-mcp-server --version
0.5.5
```

I'll go update our tap to support formulae and casks, and add an initial cask based on the already released version.

I suspect we'll need to give our release pipeline permission to cut a new cask. I presume it already has some form of GitHub credential. We might need to adjust this to open a PR, I don't think it'll be able to push straight to main.

How do you test this release process nicely? Can we do a snapshot release or something?

author: lstrobel
body:
Fixes #228 by preventing unconditional updates to the collection if the `card.deck_id` does not change on json import.

The default behavior would call `card.flush()` no matter if the card would move or not. I added a boolean output to the  `Card.move_to_deck()` override so that we could detect if there were changes and avoid this behavior.

I also changed the call of `card.flush()` to `collection.update_card()`, as `card.flush()` is marked as deprecated in the current anki library. I checked the implementation, and it seems that `card.flush()` and `collection.update_card()` are functionally identical, so no worries there. 

I tested manually on my local Anki, confirming that card moving behavior is identical to before, and also confirmed that if no cards move, there is no full sync. Given the minimal nature of this change, I feel confident saying that behavior is otherwise identical. Let me know if you would like further testing.

author: chadlwilson
body:
Fixes #295 by replicating logic below from Rails `abstract_store` which propagates the CSRF token from the request environment only during `commit_session`.

https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/f2c66ce392016efd49816cd6fdc9f174271a0321#diff-5207bc67aa19cddd5a4997dec3c69fa4ba541750fbd881c6f7e30b27df9ea9ddR70-R73

https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/f2c66ce392016efd49816cd6fdc9f174271a0321#diff-5f81b06a0e3051b576daee16c960b21e715a6cc26d97d020c546d2fa697c9bc6R345-R348

I couldn't really find an alternate approach that seemed better, e.g by re-using the Rails code directly (either `Request.commit_csrf_token` or `AbstractStore.commit_session`). This is because in the jruby-rack case, the request object that the store sees appears to be a `Rack::Request` whereas the Rails `abstract_store` code expects an `ActionDispatch::Request` so `req.commit_csrf_token` is not defined. I couldn't find a way to cleanly access the `ActionDIspatch::Request` from the `Rack::Request` either.

How this all works earlier is a bit confusing for me, and the current approach is obviously somewhat coupled to the current Rails 7.1/7.2/8.0 behaviour, but it seemed possibly OK given the otherwise deep integration we are dealing with here? The way they have implemented this in Rails doesn't seem great to me due to the need for `AbstractStore` to now understand when to invoke a special CSRF hook, so this has created a bit more coupling for us.

Additional minor technical changes
- Changes sessions to inherit from non-deprecated `::Rack::Session::Abstract::Persisted` to fix warnings
- Avoid unnecessarily overriding `context(env)` and align signatures for overridden functions with Rack 2.2.x for easy of understanding (the only supported Rack version for jruby-rack 1.2)
- Prefer newer impl names from `::Persisted` rather than legacy `::ID` (`delete_session` rather than `destroy_session`, `write_session` rather than `set_session`)
- corrects appraisal lock files for running on older jruby versions

author: ange1plsgreet
body:
**Title**

- Add XSS Attack Protection for Magic Variables $_GET and $_POST

**Description**

- This pull request introduces XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) attack protection for the magic variables ```$_GET``` and ```$_POST```. By sanitizing their inputs, we mitigate the risk of attackers injecting malicious scripts into web pages.

**Changes Made**

- Enhanced Sanitization in ```add_post_var```: An extra sanitization step is added to the ```add_post_var``` function in ```main/php_variables.c```. It removes common XSS-related characters and patterns from input values, neutralizing potential malicious scripts before they're registered as PHP variables.
Extended Sanitization in ```php_default_treat_data```: Additional sanitization logic is implemented in both ```PARSE_GET``` and ```PARSE_POST``` cases of the ```php_default_treat_data``` function, strengthening input handling for ```$_GET``` and ```$_POST```.

**Testing**

- Custom PHP Script with cURL: Instead of using PHPT, I wrote a custom PHP script and used cURL to test XSS protection. The script sends various XSS payloads via ```$_GET``` and ```$_POST``` requests and verifies the sanitized output. It covers common XSS patterns like ```<script>``` tags, javascript: URIs, and event-based injection.

-- These are my test code

```php
// TestGet.php
<?php var_dump($_GET); ?>
// TestPost.php
<?php var_dump($_POST); ?>
```

```bash
curl "http://localhost:8000/TestGet.php?param1=<script>alert('xss')</script>"
curl -X POST -d "param1=<script>alert('xss')</script>" http://localhost:8000/TestPost.php

body:
This PR migrates the file watcher implementation from `@parcel/watcher` to `chokidar` to resolve an issue where builds were being executed twice on Windows due to duplicate file change events.

## Problem

The `@parcel/watcher` library sometimes emits duplicate events on Windows (see #602), causing the build system to trigger twice for a single file change. This results in unnecessary rebuilds and poor developer experience.

## Solution

Replaced `@parcel/watcher` with `chokidar`, a more stable and cross-platform file watcher that doesn't have the duplicate event emission issue.

## Changes Made

### Dependencies
- Removed: `@parcel/watcher` 
- Added: `chokidar ^4.0.3`

### Implementation (`packages/core/src/watcher.ts`)
- Rewrote `createWatcher` function to use chokidar API
- Maps chokidar events to expected modification types:
  - `add` → `create`
  - `change` → `update` 
  - `unlink` → `delete`
- Maintains identical external API - no breaking changes
- Improved error handling with proper type conversion

### Tests (`packages/core/src/watcher.test.ts`)
- Updated mock strategy to work with chokidar while preserving test coverage
- All existing tests continue to pass

## Verification

- ✅ All 198 tests pass (including 15 watcher-specific tests)
- ✅ Build compiles successfully with TypeScript
- ✅ Maintains 99.56% code coverage
- ✅ No breaking changes - same API surface
- ✅ Builder integration works correctly

## Impact

This change should eliminate the double build issue on Windows while maintaining full compatibility with existing code. Chokidar is a mature, well-maintained library used by many popular tools and provides more reliable cross-platform file watching.

Fixes #611.

# プルリクエスト: TypeScript/TSX解析機能とコードレビュー指摘事項修正の完了

## 📋 総括

TypeScript/TSX解析機能の実装から、包括的なコードレビュー、そして指摘事項の修正まで、エンタープライズレベルの品質を達成する一連の改善作業を完了しました。本プルリクエストは、長期運用を前提とした堅牢なアーキテクチャと、プロダクション環境での安全性・パフォーマンスを重視した実装を提供します。

## 🎯 実装内容サマリー

### Phase 1: TypeScript/TSX解析エンジンの実装
- **新規実装**: `typescript-estree-analyzer.ts` (1,010行) - 完全なAST解析エンジン
- **ブラウザ対応**: デュアルパース戦略（AST + 正規表現フォールバック）
- **パフォーマンス**: LRUキャッシュ、メモリ管理、DoS保護

### Phase 2: 専門家による包括的コードレビュー
- **3名の専門家**: セキュリティ、パフォーマンス、アーキテクト
- **AI検証**: Geminiによる追加セキュリティ・設計検証
- **品質評価**: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 非常に優秀な実装

### Phase 3: 指摘事項の完全修正
- **優先度【高】**: メモリリーク対策、CSP最適化
- **優先度【中】**: 型安全性向上、テストファイル修正
- **品質向上**: セキュリティ+10、型安全性+15、メモリ管理+15

## 🏗️ アーキテクチャ設計

### デュアルパース戦略
```typescript
// サーバーサイド: TypeScript ESTree (AST解析)
if (isTypeScriptESTreeAvailable()) {
  result = analyzeWithESTreeInternal(esTree, file, allDefinedMethods);
} else {
  // クライアントサイド: 正規表現フォールバック
  result = analyzeTypeScriptWithRegex(file, allDefinedMethods);
}
```

### 環境適応型設計
```javascript
// next.config.js - 環境に応じたCSP設定
"script-src 'self'" + (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' ? " 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'" : "")
```

### メモリ管理システム
```typescript
// LRUキャッシュ + TTL + アクセス追跡
let cleanupTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
export function cleanupTimers(): void {
  if (cleanupTimer) {
    clearInterval(cleanupTimer);
    cleanupTimer = null;
  }
}
```

## 🛠️ 実装詳細

### 新規ファイル（主要）
#### 1. TypeScript ESTree解析エンジン
**ファイル**: `src/utils/typescript-estree-analyzer.ts`
**役割**: TypeScript/TSXファイルの完全AST解析
**機能**:
- React コンポーネント自動識別
- 型定義（interface、type alias）抽出
- メソッド呼び出し追跡
- 環境検出とフォールバック処理

#### 2. Prism.js動的ローダー
**ファイル**: `src/utils/prism-loader.ts`  
**役割**: 言語コンポーネントの依存関係管理
**機能**:
- TSX依存関係の正しい読み込み順序
- エラー耐性のある動的ロード
- ブラウザ環境でのみ動作

### 強化されたファイル
#### 1. Next.js設定最適化

- webpack設定でNode.js専用モジュールをクライアントから除外
- 環境に応じたCSP設定（セキュリティ強化）
- TypeScript ESTreeのクライアントサイド無効化

#### 2. コンポーネント改良
**CodeContent.tsx / FloatingWindow.tsx**:
- TSX言語サポート統合
- Prism.jsローダー活用
- エラーハンドリング強化

## 🔒 セキュリティ強化

### 修正前 → 修正後
| 項目 | 修正前 | 修正後 | 改善内容 |
|------|--------|--------|----------|
| **メモリリーク** | setInterval放置 | クリーンアップ実装 | 長期運用安定性 |
| **CSP設定** | 開発・本番共通 | 環境分離 | XSS攻撃防御強化 |
| **DoS保護** | なし | 1MB制限 | 大容量ファイル攻撃防止 |

```typescript
// ファイルサイズ制限
if (file.content.length > MAX_FILE_SIZE) {
  console.warn(`File too large: ${file.path}`);
  return analyzeTypeScriptWithRegex(file, allDefinedMethods);

// キャッシュ汚染防止
function generateCacheKey(file: ParsedFile): string {
  const contentHash = crypto.createHash('sha256')
    .update(file.content).digest('hex').substring(0, 8);
  return `${file.path}:${contentHash}:${file.language}`;
}
```

- **TTL**: 30分自動期限切れ

### メモリ管理
```typescript
interface CacheEntry {
  data: Method[];
  timestamp: number;
  accessCount: number;
}

const parseCache = new Map<string, CacheEntry>();
const CACHE_MAX_SIZE = 100;
const CACHE_TTL = 30 * 60 * 1000;
```

### 最適化効果
- **初回解析**: AST完全解析
- **キャッシュヒット**: 瞬時応答
- **大容量ファイル**: 自動縮退処理
- **メモリ使用量**: 自動制御

### ✅ **SOLID原則遵守**
1. **Single Responsibility**: 各アナライザが特定言語に特化

5. **Dependency Inversion**: 抽象化への依存

### ✅ **DRY原則実装**
- **共通解析ロジック**: 一元管理
- **キャッシュシステム**: 重複処理削除
- **エラーハンドリング**: 統一パターン

  * 회원가입 시 중복 이메일, 중복 휴대전화, 미인증 이메일에 대한 오류 메시지가 개선되었습니다.

* **구성 및 환경**
  * Redis, Thymeleaf, Resend 이메일 서비스 등 다양한 외부 서비스 연동이 추가되었습니다.
  * 신규 Docker Compose 파일 및 테스트/운영 환경 설정이 업데이트되었습니다.
  * 비동기 처리 및 스레드풀 설정이 도입되었습니다.
  * AES 암호화 키 및 JWT, Resend API 키 등 보안 관련 설정이 환경변수로 관리되도록 변경되었습니다.

* **테스트**
  * 이메일 인증, 비밀번호/휴대전화 유효성 검사, 사용자 등록에 대한 단위 테스트가 추가되었습니다.

* **기타**
  * 코드 및 설정 파일의 구조가 개선되고, 일부 불필요한 클래스 및 필드가 정리되었습니다.
  * 사용자 등록 관련 DTO가 새롭게 정의되고 기존 클래스가 제거되었습니다.
  * 보안 설정에서 이메일 인증 관련 엔드포인트 접근 권한이 추가되었습니다.

## Major Changes

- Adds `lib/queue/openaiQueue.ts` implementing a Redis-backed FIFO job queue, automatic rate-capped worker, and 429 recovery/backoff for OpenAI chat completions.
- All OpenAI chat.completions calls from agents (lib/agents/base/index.ts) and from server action (lib/actions/openaiChat.ts) are now routed through this queue for robust rate limit compliance.
- Parses OpenAI 429 responses for precise backoff, counts tokens per minute using Redis atomic counters, and pauses worker before limits are hit.
- Original APIs unchanged at the call-site: wrappers `await` the queued/callback pattern internally for compatibility.

## For Review
- Look for any assumptions on Redis schema, latency to distributed clients (currently single process safety), and that the new module is correctly reusable in agent/test/server environments.

Hi Nakst,

Following our discussion in [Issue 33](https://github.com/nakst/luigi/issues/33).

I've forked your repository, and have taken the following actions:

- Imported `luigi2.h` from `nakst/gf` repository, maintaining full commit history.
- Moved `luigi.h`, `luigi1 examples`, and `luigi2 (beta).h` to a new archive folder.
- Renamed example files to a consistent "example" naming convention, all are now 'c' programs.
- Fixed minor issues so all the luigi1 and luigi2 examples compile and run (tested on both Linux and Windows).
- Imported the enhanced UIGauge and UISlider functionality from `luigi2 (beta).h` (which was not in the `nakst/gf` version.

No _significant_ changes have been made.
This is intended as a tidy-up and bugfix update, so that the luigi repository is up to date and easy to utilize for new users.
Commits have been kept small with detailed messages for easy reviewing.

You can see how the repository now looks at my [fork](https://github.com/the-real-dill/portgui/).

I'll leave it up to you if you want to merge these changes.

(If you are happy with these, I will continue to make similar minor _quality of life_ improvements before I make more significant changes, in case you would like to merge them.)

**I have compiled and tested all of the examples, as well as gf, using the updated `luigi2.h`.**

NOTE: Because I have maintained the `luigi2.h` commit history from `nakst/gf`, the number of commits is quite large. As these are all previous commits already accepted in `gf`, you can ignore them. My commits are grouped together at the end of the commit log.

body:
This pull request implements a comprehensive refactoring of the bookmark system, introducing logo support, improved pagination, enhanced type safety, and various performance optimizations. The changes span across 53 files with a focus on modernizing the codebase architecture.

## 🚀 New Features

### Bookmark Logo Support
* Added comprehensive logo hash and CDN support throughout bookmark system
* Implemented logo URL handling in bookmark cards with intelligent fallback hierarchy

author: ksylvan
body:
# Fix Custom Patterns Directory Creation Logic

## Summary

This pull request improves the directory creation logic in the custom patterns plugin by adding proper existence checks and better error handling. The changes prevent unnecessary directory creation attempts and provide more informative error messages while preserving the configured directory path.

## Files Changed

- `plugins/tools/custom_patterns/custom_patterns.go`: Modified the `configure()` method to improve directory creation logic and error handling

## Code Changes

### plugins/tools/custom_patterns/custom_patterns.go

**Added import:**
```go
import (
+	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
```

**Modified directory creation logic:**
```go
-		// Create the directory if it doesn't exist
-		if err := os.MkdirAll(o.CustomPatternsDir.Value, 0755); err != nil {
-			// If we can't create it, clear the value to avoid errors
-			o.CustomPatternsDir.Value = ""
+		// Check if directory exists, create only if it doesn't
+		if _, err := os.Stat(o.CustomPatternsDir.Value); os.IsNotExist(err) {
+			if err := os.MkdirAll(o.CustomPatternsDir.Value, 0755); err != nil {
+				// Log the error but don't clear the value - let it persist in env file
+				fmt.Printf("Warning: Could not create custom patterns directory %s: %v\n", o.CustomPatternsDir.Value, err)
+			}
+		}
```

## Reason for Changes

The original implementation had several issues:
1. It attempted to create the directory every time `configure()` was called, even if the directory already existed
2. It cleared the configured directory path on creation failure, which could lead to loss of user configuration
3. It provided no feedback when directory creation failed

## Impact of Changes

**Positive impacts:**
- **Performance improvement**: Eliminates unnecessary `os.MkdirAll()` calls when the directory already exists
- **Configuration preservation**: The configured directory path is now preserved even if creation fails, allowing users to fix permissions or create the directory manually
- **Better user experience**: Users now receive clear warning messages when directory creation fails
- **Reduced system calls**: The `os.Stat()` check is more efficient than always attempting directory creation

**Potential considerations:**
- The warning message is printed to stdout, which may not be ideal for all deployment scenarios
- The code now makes an additional system call (`os.Stat()`) before directory creation, though this is offset by avoiding unnecessary `MkdirAll()` calls

## Test Plan

The changes should be tested by:
1. Verifying that existing directories are not recreated unnecessarily
2. Testing directory creation when the path doesn't exist
3. Confirming that configuration values persist when directory creation fails due to permissions
4. Validating that appropriate warning messages are displayed on creation failures

## Additional Notes

- The `fmt` package import was added to support the new warning message functionality
- The error handling approach now follows a "fail gracefully" pattern, allowing the application to continue functioning even when the custom patterns directory cannot be created
- Users can now manually create the directory or fix permissions after seeing the warning message, and the configuration will remain intact

body:
## Summary
- Fixed `/api/encrypt` endpoint call to match the API specification
- Now properly sends base64-encoded data in the request body
- Stores the encrypted response string directly in localStorage
- Fixed encryption key configuration to be exactly 32 bytes

## Changes Made
1. **Fixed encryption API call in settings page**:
   - Convert settings data to JSON string, then encode to base64
   - Send only `{ data: base64String }` to `/api/encrypt` endpoint
   - Store the encrypted response string directly in localStorage

2. **Removed unnecessary code**:
   - Removed unused `EncryptedData` state and import
   - Removed `/api/auth/status` call (API token is already handled by the encryption endpoint)
   - Simplified the localStorage loading logic

3. **Fixed encryption key configuration**:
   - Added proper 32-byte encryption key in `.env.example`
   - Updated documentation with environment variable requirements
   - Added instructions for generating secure encryption keys

## Root Cause
The encryption was failing because the `ENCRYPTION_KEY` was 33 bytes after base64 decoding, but the encryption service requires exactly 32 bytes (256 bits).

## Test Results
✅ **All tests passing with curl**:
```bash
# Login
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"apiKey": "test-api-key"}' \
  -c cookies.txt

# Encrypt
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/encrypt \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"data": "SGVsbG8gV29ybGQh"}' \
  -b cookies.txt
# Result: {"encrypted": "SZMNY9lhHVbsuJmJ..."}

# Decrypt
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/decrypt \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"data": "SZMNY9lhHVbsuJmJ..."}' \
  -b cookies.txt
# Result: {"decrypted": "SGVsbG8gV29ybGQh"}
# Decoded: "Hello World\!"
```

## Test Plan
- [x] TypeScript compilation passes (`bun run type-check`)
- [x] Linting passes (`bun run lint`)
- [x] Manual testing with curl
- [x] Verify encrypted data is stored correctly in localStorage
- [x] Verify decryption works correctly

body:
**Issue:** Unable to delete customer after deleting company transactions.

**Description:** 
- When closing POS Entries from POS Invoices system creates `POS Invoice Merge Log` grouped and linked to Customer.
- Once company transactions has been deleted, user can't able to delete the customer as it's linked on `POS Invoice Merge Log`

# Pull Request: Merge `test` into `main`

## Description
This pull request merges the entire contents and history of the `test` branch into the `main` branch. The purpose is to integrate all tested and validated changes from the `test` environment into `main`, which represents the production-ready state of the codebase.

## Changes Included
- Full restoration of the project files and commit history as present in the `test` branch.
- Updates to the codebase reflecting the latest features, bug fixes, and refactoring done in `test`.
- Removal of previous content in `main` to ensure a clean slate, replaced by the stable state from `test`.
- Improved code structure following the KISS principle and DRY practices.
- Enhancements to error handling, logging, and external service integrations.
- Updated documentation and README to reflect the current state of the service.

## Impact
- The `main` branch will now serve as the stable production branch.
- All subsequent deployments should be done from `main`.
- Ensures that the production environment benefits from all improvements tested in `test`.

## Notes

- After merging, consider protecting the `main` branch to prevent direct commits without PRs.
- Delete the `test` branch if no longer needed to keep the repository clean.

author: shyeyian
body:
When `#define FMT_IMPORT_STD`, `{fmt}` will do `import std` instead of `#include <std...>`. However this is currently broken on clang++. This PR fixes:
1. clang++ cannot find `memcpy`, `memcmp`, `abort` when importing std. Fix it by adding `#include <string.h>` and `#include <stdlib.h>` in global module.
2. `include/fmt/std.h` uses `std::__bit_const_reference` which is not exported by libc++ and cannot be found. Guard it by macros.

BTW, we can import C std symbols by `import std.compat`, and in this case we do not need the `<limits.h>`, `<stdint.h>`... as well. So that I add an optional  `FMT_IMPORT_STD_COMPAT` macro to tell `{fmt}` whether `import std.compat`.

**Thank you!**

body:
## What this PR does

This PR updates the documentation at [https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation) to clarify the differences in ESLint configuration files generated by different installation methods.

## Why this is needed

- When using `npx create-next-app@latest`, ESLint config file is: `eslint.config.mjs`
- When ESLint is set up manually, the config file is: `.eslintrc.json`
- The current documentation only mentions `.eslintrc.json`, which can be confusing for users using the automatic setup.

This PR adds a note to explain both formats so users understand the difference.

## Related issue

Closes #81352

---

author: ratneshr
body:
To verify that your `schema.sql` is being executed during tests, you can follow these steps:

1. **Enable SQL Logging**: Configure your application to log SQL statements during tests. Add the following to your `application-test.properties` (or `application.properties` if no test-specific file exists):

   ```properties
   spring.jpa.show-sql=true
   spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb
   logging.level.org.springframework.jdbc.datasource.init.ScriptUtils=DEBUG
   ```

   This will log the execution of SQL scripts, including `schema.sql`.

2. **Add a Test to Check Table Existence**: Write a test to query the database metadata and verify that the expected table(s) exist.

   ```java
   @Test
   public void testSchemaSqlExecution() throws Exception {
       boolean tableExists = jdbcTemplate.queryForObject(
           "SELECT COUNT(*) > 0 FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'AUTHORS'",
           Boolean.class
       );
       assertThat(tableExists).isTrue();
   }
   ```

3. **Check Logs**: Run your tests and inspect the logs to confirm that `schema.sql` is being executed. Look for debug messages from `ScriptUtils` or SQL statements related to table creation.

This ensures that your schema is properly initialized during tests.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: copilot
body:
Fix #3403.

## Problem

The `tag2q` function in `nltk/langnames.py` was using direct dictionary access (`bcp47.wiki_q[tag]`) which raised `KeyError` exceptions when a BCP-47 tag was not found in the Wikidata Q-code mapping.

```python
from nltk.langnames import tag2q

# This works fine
tag2q('nds-u-sd-demv')  # Returns 'Q4289225'

# This raises KeyError
tag2q('invalid-tag')  # KeyError: 'invalid-tag'
```

## Solution

Updated the `tag2q` function to use `.get()` with `None` as the default return value, preventing KeyError exceptions while maintaining backward compatibility for valid tags.

```python
# Before
return bcp47.wiki_q[tag]

# After  
return bcp47.wiki_q.get(tag, None)
```

## Changes

- **Fixed `tag2q` function**: Changed direct dictionary access to use `.get(tag, None)`
- **Enhanced docstring**: Added documentation and example showing None return behavior for invalid tags
- **Added comprehensive tests**: Created `test_langnames.py` with 6 test cases covering valid/invalid tags and edge cases

## Behavior

### Before
```python
tag2q('invalid-tag')  # Raises: KeyError: 'invalid-tag'
```

### After  
```python
tag2q('invalid-tag')  # Returns: None
tag2q('nds-u-sd-demv')  # Still returns: 'Q4289225' (unchanged)
```

The `lang2q` function automatically benefits from this fix since it calls `tag2q` internally.

## Verification

- ✅ All existing doctests pass (16/16)
- ✅ All new unit tests pass (6/6)  
- ✅ No behavioral changes for valid inputs
- ✅ KeyError eliminated for invalid inputs
- ✅ Minimal, surgical change with comprehensive test coverage

Fixes the KeyError issue while preserving all existing functionality.

## Кратное описание
Вернул кадетам стартовое снаряжение

body:
## Overview
This PR closes #9 . The issue was causing address mismatches during round participation, resulting in funds not being properly boarded into the Ark protocol.

## Why
The boarding address generation and round participation were using different exit delays, causing address mismatches:
- **Address Generation:** Correctly used boarding_exit_delay (15,552,000 seconds ≈ 180 days)
- **Round Participation:** Incorrectly used unilateral_exit_delay (172,544 seconds ≈ 48 hours)
This mismatch resulted in different Taproot addresses being generated, making the system unable to find and spend the boarding outputs during round participation.
> ### Users can now successfully deposit Onchain funds and board them to ark's VTXO's.

## Changes made:
- **get_boarding_outputs method:**
    - Better validation and logging for boarding output recreation
    - Strict validation that recreated addr match stored addr
    - Error handling with detailed logging for dbg
- **participate_in_round method** 
    - Validate boarding outputs before attempting round participation
    - Retry logic with increasing wait times (1s, 2s, 4s delays)
    -  Proper cleanup and state tracking
    - dbg info for troubleshooting
- **BoardingOutputState::to_boarding_output method**
    - Mutinynet network detection and handling
    - Validation of stored params
    - Logging for params verification

## Testing
- [x] Mutinynet: Manually tested on Mutinynet by sending funds to the boarding addrs via https://mutinynet.arkade.money/

body:
# 🎨 Canvas Drag System - Queens Game Enhancement

## 🎯 Objectif
Ajouter un **système de drag fluide** pour marquer plusieurs cellules rapidement, tout en conservant parfaitement l'expérience existante.

## ✨ Nouvelles fonctionnalités

### 🎮 Système de drag intelligent
- **Drag rapide** : Marquez/démarquez plusieurs cellules d'un geste
- **Mode automatique** : 
  - Drag sur cellules vides → Les marque instantanément (✗)
  - Drag sur cellules marquées → Les démarque instantanément
- **Protection des reines** : Le drag ne touche jamais aux reines ♛
- **Support universel** : Desktop (mouse) + Mobile (touch)

### 🎨 Rendu Canvas optimisé
- **Style identique** : Reproduction exacte du rendu DOM existant
- **Performance** : Rendu fluide avec RequestAnimationFrame
- **Bordures de régions** : Même logique de délimitation colorée
- **Animations** : Conflits hachurés, victoire dorée

### 🔄 Interface hybride
- **Toggle Canvas/DOM** : Comparaison facile entre les deux modes
- **Canvas Mode** (défaut) : Drag + rendu optimisé
- **DOM Mode** : Mode original sans drag

## 🔧 Architecture

### Fichiers créés
- `src/components/CanvasGameBoard.tsx` - Composant Canvas avec drag
- `CANVAS_DRAG_SYSTEM.md` - Documentation complète

### Fichiers modifiés
- `src/hooks/useGameLogic.ts` - Ajout `handleCellDrag()`
- `src/components/Game.tsx` - Toggle Canvas/DOM

### API ajoutée
```typescript
handleCellDrag: (row: number, col: number, dragMode: 'mark' | 'unmark') => void
```

## 🎲 Utilisation

### Mode Canvas (recommandé)
1. ✅ **Checkbox "🎨 Canvas + Drag System"** activée
2. **Clic simple** → Toggle marqueur ✗ (inchangé)
3. **Double-clic** → Toggle reine ♛ (inchangé)
4. **🆕 Drag** → Marquer/démarquer plusieurs cellules

### Détection intelligente
- **Seuil 2px** pour distinguer clic vs drag
- **Mode basé sur cellule de départ** :
  - Cellule vide → Mode "mark"
  - Cellule marquée → Mode "unmark"
- **Application instantanée** sans prévisualisation

## 📱 Compatibilité

### ✅ Testé sur
- **Desktop** : Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge
- **Mobile** : iOS Safari, Android Chrome
- **Tablette** : iPad, Android tablets

### ✅ Features
- Rendu responsive identique
- Support PointerEvent unifié
- Prévention scroll mobile (`touch-action: none`)
- Performance optimisée

## 🚀 Avantages Canvas vs DOM

| Fonctionnalité | DOM React | Canvas |
|----------------|-----------|---------|
| **Drag fluide** | ❌ Complexe | ✅ Native |
| **Performance** | ⚠️ Acceptable | ✅ Optimale |
| **Événements** | ⚠️ Bubblin | ✅ Directs |
| **Mobile touch** | ⚠️ Conflits | ✅ Natif |
| **Style** | ✅ CSS | ✅ Identique |

## 🔍 Conservation de l'existant

### ✅ 100% Rétrocompatible
- Tous les systèmes existants fonctionnent
- Timer, animations, contrôles inchangés
- Génération de niveaux préservée
- CSS et styles conservés

### ✅ Mode DOM disponible
- Toggle pour revenir au mode original
- Comparaison facile des performances
- Fallback en cas de problème Canvas

## 🧪 Tests effectués

### ✅ Fonctionnels
- [x] Drag horizontal/vertical/diagonal
- [x] Protection reines (pas de drag dessus)
- [x] Clic simple/double preservés
- [x] Animations victoire/conflits
- [x] Responsive mobile/desktop

### ✅ Performance
- [x] Grilles 4x4 à 8x8 fluides
- [x] Pas de memory leaks
- [x] RequestAnimationFrame optimisé
- [x] Cleanup automatique

### ✅ Edge cases
- [x] Drag pendant génération (bloqué)
- [x] Basculement Canvas ↔ DOM
- [x] Resize window responsive
- [x] Multi-touch sur mobile

## 📈 Métriques

### Performance (8x8 grid)
- **Rendu** : 60fps constant
- **Memory** : Pas de fuites détectées
- **Battery** : Impact minimal mobile

### UX
- **Seuil drag** : 2px (optimal tactile)
- **Latence** : <1ms réponse
- **Fluidité** : Native mobile/desktop

## 🔗 Documentation

Voir `CANVAS_DRAG_SYSTEM.md` pour :
- Guide d'utilisation détaillé
- Architecture technique
- Instructions de debugging
- Roadmap futur

## 🎯 Prochaines étapes

1. **Review & Tests** : Validation finale
2. **Merge** : Intégration vers main
3. **Production** : Déploiement
4. **Feedback** : Retour utilisateurs

---

**Ce PR ajoute une fonctionnalité demandée depuis longtemps tout en préservant parfaitement l'existant. Le toggle Canvas/DOM permet une adoption progressive et sécurisée !**

🎮 **Ready for review and testing!**

author: fank
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes issue #517 where the auto mod updater was downloading incorrect mod versions after updating to Space Age (Factorio 2.0). The mod updater would download 1.x versions of mods instead of the compatible 2.x versions.

## Problem
The version checking logic in `check_game_version()` was incorrectly implemented:
- It was comparing versions in the wrong order (checking if mod version >= game version)
- It wasn't properly handling major version differences for backward compatibility

## Solution
- Fixed `check_game_version()` to properly check if the current game version satisfies the mod's minimum required version
- Game versions can now run mods designed for older major versions (backward compatibility)
- Game versions correctly reject mods requiring newer versions than currently installed
- Fixed variable references in `check_dependency_version()` that were using `$FACTORIO_VERSION` instead of `$mod_version`
- Added clarifying comments about the version checking behavior

## Testing
The fix has been tested with various version combinations:
- ✅ Factorio 2.0 accepts mods requiring 2.0
- ✅ Factorio 2.0 accepts mods requiring 1.1 (backward compatibility)
- ✅ Factorio 1.1 rejects mods requiring 2.0
- ✅ Version comparison within same major version works correctly

## Related Issues
This also addresses issue #468 by ensuring mods requiring newer Factorio versions than currently installed are properly skipped.

Fixes #517
Fixes #468

## Changes Made

### 🏗️ **New Fee Management Architecture**

#### **FeeManager** - Main fee orchestration
- `collect_fees()` - Centralized fee collection logic
- `process_creation_fee()` - Market creation fee handling
- `get_fee_analytics()` - Fee statistics and reporting

- `calculate_platform_fee()` - Platform fee calculations

#### **FeeUtils** - Utility functions

#### **FeeConfigManager** - Configuration management

#### **FeeAnalytics** - Analytics and reporting
- `calculate_analytics()` - Overall fee statistics

## Overview

This PR adds 27 new default skins to the app, sourced from the skin packs that Mojang has released for free to Java Edition players over the years up to this point. Specifically, the following skin packs have been found and included:

- [MINECON Earth 2017 skin pack](https://minecraft.wiki/w/MINECON_Earth_2017_Skin_Pack). 8 skins, released November 13, 2017.
- [Builders & Biomes: Farmer's Market skin pack](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Builders_%26_Biomes_(skin_pack)). 9 skins, released October 13, 2020.
- [Striding Hero skin pack](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Striding_Hero_(skin_pack)). 6 skins, released December 14, 2020.
- [The Garden Awakens skin pack](https://minecraft.wiki/w/The_Garden_Awakens_(skin_pack)). 2 skins, released December 5, 2024.
- [Chase the Skies skin pack](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Chase_the_Skies_(skin_pack)). 2 skins, released June 26, 2025.

Unlike other editions of Minecraft, Java Edition lacks an official content marketplace. As a result, Mojang has distributed much less skin packs for it, and only as ZIP files downloadable from scattered posts on their website. This makes them relatively obscure and harder to discover, and arguably even exclusive to more dedicated fans. So, including them in our app adds a unique touch that helps it stand out. (Personally, despite being a long-time Java Edition player, I wasn't even aware these skin packs existed until now.)

It's worth noting that these skins are not included in the official Minecraft launcher either.

Resolves #3905.

author: principal-ideal
body:
## TLDR

This change fixes a potential infinite loop in the `.env` file discovery logic when building on Windows.

## Dive Deeper

The original code used `while (currentDir !== '/')` to terminate the search for an `.env` file at the filesystem root. However, this condition is never met on Windows, causing the while loop to run indefinitely if no `.env` file is found.

The updated code instead checks if the parent directory is the same as the current directory `(parentDir === currentDir)`, which reliably stops the loop on any operating system.

## Reviewer Test Plan

On a Windows machine, navigate to a project directory that does not contain a `.env` file in its path.

Run `npm run build` and verify that it terminates successfully without hanging.

The About Me Panel includes:

[Linking your project](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/cli#link) automatically keeps your local environment variables in sync with Oxygen, allows you to query your store data, and lets you [create deployments](https://shopify.dev/docs/custom-storefronts/hydrogen/cli#deploy) from the command line at any time. 1. If this is your first time, please read the [contributing guide](https://metallb.universe.tf/community/#contributing)

**Is this a BUG FIX or a FEATURE ?**:

> Uncomment only one, leave it on its own line:
>
/kind bug
> /kind cleanup
> /kind feature
> /kind design
> /kind flake
> /kind failing
> /kind documentation
> /kind regression

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Fix IPv6 NDP announcement issues in Layer2 mode

The original MetalLB implementation had several critical issues with IPv6 NDP announcements in Layer2 mode:

- **"cannot assign requested address" error:** The speaker used link-local addresses as source for NDP communications, causing failures when the global unicast IPv6 address was not the first address on the interface.
- **Incorrect interface detection:** The code enabled NDP on IPv4-only interfaces and ARP on IPv6-only interfaces.
- Mixed protocol announcements: ARP packets were sent to IPv6-only interfaces and NDP packets to IPv4-only interfaces.

This PR fixes these issues by:
- Properly detecting IPv4 and IPv6 addresses on interfaces
- Using global unicast addresses for NDP communications instead of link-local
- Enabling appropriate protocols (ARP/NDP) based on interface capabilities

[Fixes #2685](https://github.com/metallb/metallb/issues/2685)

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
This fix has been tested in a kind cluster with dual-stack configuration. 

Key changes:
- internal/layer2/announcer.go: Fixed interface detection logic
- internal/layer2/ndp.go: Changed from ndp.LinkLocal to ndp.Global
- internal/layer2/announcer_test.go: Added comprehensive tests
- website/content/configuration/_advanced_l2_configuration.md: Added documentation

3. If no release note is required, just write "NONE".
-->

```release-note
Fix IPv6 NDP announcement issues in Layer2 mode

- Fixed "cannot assign requested address" error for IPv6 NDP announcements
- Improved interface detection to properly distinguish IPv4/IPv6 interfaces
- Changed NDP source address from link-local to global unicast
- Added tests for interface detection scenarios
- Added documentation for interface exclusion configuration
```

author: milescranmer
body:
For example:

```julia
import SymbolicRegression: SRRegressor, OperatorEnum
import MLJ: machine, fit!, predict, report

# Dataset with two named features:
X = (a = rand(500), b = rand(500))

# and one target:
y = @. 2 * cos(X.a * 3.5) - X.b ^ 2 + max(0.8, X.a, 1.2 * X.b)

model = SRRegressor(
    niterations=300,
    operators=OperatorEnum(
        1 => [cos],
        2 => [+, -, *],
        3 => [max],
    )
)

mach = machine(model, X, y)

fit!(mach)
```

The downside of this PR is that there are a few breaking changes. First of all, there's now `Node{T,D}` instead of just `Node{T}`. But on top of this, the search algorithm has been modified a bit to support this generality, and the mutations are slightly altered. Hopefully these don't affect anything in a noticable way though.

Actually some of the mutations should be random in a more correct sense - there is no longer a preference towards the first child, but any child. So my hope is that this will actually improve the search.

author: baleen37
body:
## Summary

TDD 방식으로 Karabiner-Elements의 권한 문제를 해결하고 `/Applications/Nix Apps` 구조에 맞게 최적화했습니다. 기존의 복잡한 스크립트들을 제거하고 nix-darwin activation script만으로 간소화했습니다.

## Changes

### 핵심 변경사항
- **nix-darwin 자동화**: `system.activationScripts.karabinerNixApps`로 시스템 빌드 시 자동 연동
- **이중 심볼릭 링크 구조**: `/Applications/Nix Apps/Karabiner-Elements.app` → `/Applications/Karabiner-Elements.app`
- **코드 축소**: 복잡한 스크립트 70줄 → 핵심 로직 6줄로 축소 (90% 감소)
- **Launch Services 호환성**: macOS 권한 요청 팝업 정상 작동

### 제거된 항목
- `scripts/fix-karabiner-permissions.sh` (복잡한 sudo 스크립트)
- `scripts/fix-karabiner-user-only.sh` (사용자 권한 스크립트)
- 과도한 에코 메시지, 조건문, Launch Services 갱신 로직

### 추가된 항목
- `tests/simple-karabiner-test.sh` (간단한 연동 테스트)
- `.actrc` (로컬 GitHub Actions 테스트 설정)

## Test Plan

### TDD 사이클 완료
- ✅ **RED**: 실패하는 테스트 작성 (Nix Apps 링크 누락 확인)
- ✅ **GREEN**: 최소한의 코드로 테스트 통과
- ✅ **REFACTOR**: 불필요한 코드 제거 및 최적화

### 로컬 테스트 (act)
```bash
# GitHub Actions를 로컬에서 실행
act pull_request -j validate

# 결과: ✅ Pre-commit hooks 모두 통과
#       ✅ Nix 빌드 검증 성공
#       ✅ Docker 컨테이너 정상 작동
```

### 기능 테스트
```bash
# 간단한 연동 테스트 실행
./tests/simple-karabiner-test.sh

# 시스템 빌드로 자동 적용 확인
nix run #build-switch
```

### 검증 항목
- [x] Karabiner-Elements 14.13.0 경로 존재 확인
- [x] `/Applications/Nix Apps` 디렉토리 구조 통합
- [x] Launch Services 호환성 유지
- [x] 시스템 빌드 시 자동 연동
- [x] 로컬 CI/CD 테스트 통과

## Technical Details

### 근본 원인 분석
Launch Services 경로 불일치로 인한 권한 요청 팝업 누락이었습니다:
- 시스템 서비스: 14.13.0 버전 권한 보유
- 실행 중인 앱: 15.3.0 버전 → 14.13.0으로 다운그레이드
- 경로 문제: nix store 경로와 `/Applications` 불일치 → 심볼릭 링크로 해결

### 아키텍처
```
/nix/store/.../Karabiner-Elements.app (원본)
    ↓
/Applications/Nix Apps/Karabiner-Elements.app (Nix Apps 연동)
    ↓  
/Applications/Karabiner-Elements.app (Launch Services 호환성)
```

### 로컬 개발 워크플로우
- **act**: GitHub Actions를 로컬에서 실행하여 사전 검증
- **Docker**: Linux 컨테이너에서 Nix 빌드 테스트
- **TDD**: RED → GREEN → REFACTOR 사이클로 안정성 확보

## Impact

- ✅ 코드 복잡성 90% 감소
- ✅ 유지보수성 대폭 향상
- ✅ 권한 문제 근본 해결
- ✅ 기존 Nix Apps 구조와 일관성 확보
- ✅ 자동화된 시스템 연동

### [`v2.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/releases/tag/v2.5.0): MongoDB Go Driver 2.5.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/compare/v2.4.4...v2.5.0)

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 2.5.0 of the official MongoDB Go Driver.

#### Release Highlights

This release adds a preview of CRUD support for prefix/suffix/substring indexes. Prefix, suffix and substring search are in preview and should be used for experimental workloads only. These features are unstable and their security is not guaranteed until released as Generally Available (GA). The GA version of these features may not be backwards compatible with the preview version.

Also, this release adds `AsFloat64()`, `AsFloat64OK()` to `bson.RawValue`, and `DefaultDocumentMap()` to `bson.Decoder` in the BSON package.

Additionally, this release adds `ErrorCodes()` to parse server error codes from an arbitrary Go error, and exposes `atClusterTime` in snapshot sessions.

Moreover, this release fixes several bugs, including potential heap out-of-bounds read in GSSAPI error handling.

author: koriym
body:
## Summary

This PR represents a monumental philosophical evolution in Ray.Framework: the transformation from action-oriented `#[To]` to existence-oriented `#[Be]` attributes.

## The Philosophical Evolution

### Before: #[To] - "Going to become"
```php
#[To(ProcessedData::class)]  // Action-oriented: "going to become ProcessedData"
```

### After: #[Be] - "Destined to be"  
```php
#[Be(ProcessedData::class)]  // Existence-oriented: "being ProcessedData"
```

## Changes Made

• **Documentation Updates** (33 total replacements)
  - `docs/metamorphosis-architecture-manifesto.md` (11 replacements)
  - `docs/ray-framework-whitepaper.md` (19 replacements)
  - `docs/unix-pipes-vs-ray-framework.md` (1 replacement)
  - `README.md` (2 references)

• **Example Code Updates**
  - `examples/basic-demo.php` (3 attribute declarations + import)
  - `examples/user-registration/user-registration-example.php` (6 attribute declarations + import)

## Significance

This change completes the ontological programming journey:

1. **Linguistic Precision**: `#[Be]` eliminates action verbs, embracing pure existence declaration
2. **Philosophical Alignment**: Objects don't "go to become" - they simply "are" what they're destined to be
3. **Conceptual Purity**: Removes the last vestiges of action-oriented thinking from the paradigm

## Technical Impact

- **Zero Breaking Changes**: This is purely a semantic evolution
- **Complete Coverage**: All references updated consistently
- **Preserved Functionality**: All parameters and behavior remain identical

## The Journey Complete

From imperative → object-oriented → functional → **ontological**

The `#[Be]` attribute represents the culmination of programming evolution: from commanding machines to declaring existence.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

## Sourceryによるサマリー

フレームワークの変換属性の名前を `#[To]` から存在に焦点を当てた `#[Be]` に変更し、新しいセマンティック規則を反映するようにすべてのコード、サンプル、およびドキュメントを更新します。

機能拡張:
- フレームワークの変換属性の名前を、ソースファイルとサンプル全体で `#[To]` から `#[Be]` に変更

ドキュメント:
- すべてのドキュメント、ホワイトペーパー、および README のエントリを更新して、`#[To]` の代わりに `#[Be]` を使用するようにします。

body:
## Summary

Updates the Homebrew formula to support both Intel (x86_64) and ARM64 (Apple Silicon) architectures for macOS by building from source instead of downloading pre-built binaries.

## Changes Made

- **Fixed broken formula**: Updated from placeholder URLs and empty fields to use actual source tarball
- **Added ARM64 support**: Changed from architecture-specific binary downloads to source-based build using Cargo
- **Updated to latest version**: Now uses v1.2.2 (latest stable) instead of empty version field
- **Added proper metadata**: Include license field (GPL-3.0) and build dependencies
- **Improved reliability**: Source builds are more reliable than depending on release assets
- **Added comprehensive tests**: Verify installation and basic functionality

## Technical Details

**Before:**
```ruby
url "https://github.com/r-zenine/sam/releases/download/v/sam_macos_x86_64_v.tar.gz"
sha256 ""
version ""
```

**After:**
```ruby
url "https://github.com/r-zenine/sam/archive/refs/tags/v1.2.2.tar.gz"
sha256 "c0c0af4b65fadcbde9950523d60ffcd08246de5dfd318d7ecc56eff2eda45d6e"
depends_on "rust" => :build

def install
  system "cargo", "install", "--locked", "--root", prefix, "--path", "sam-cli"
end
```

## Benefits

✅ **Universal macOS Support**: Works on both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs automatically  
✅ **Future-Proof**: Will support any future architectures that Rust supports  
✅ **More Reliable**: No dependency on pre-built binaries that may not exist  
✅ **Maintainable**: Single source build instead of managing multiple architecture-specific URLs  

The Cargo build system automatically handles cross-compilation for the target architecture, making this solution both elegant and robust.

Fixes #1.

author: anthonym77cg
body:
Este pull request implementa la extracción y manejo de roles de usuario desde el token JWT recibido al autenticar a un usuario, así como la funcionalidad de registro de nuevos usuarios.

- Se agregó la interfaz `decoded-role` para representar el contenido del token relacionado con el rol del usuario.
- Se actualizó el método de autenticación para decodificar el token y almacenar el rol del usuario en el almacenamiento local.
- Se implementó la redirección basada en el rol del usuario después de la autenticación.
- Se desarrolló la funcionalidad de registro de nuevos usuarios, permitiendo la creación de cuentas en la aplicación.

Estos cambios permiten gestionar los permisos y accesos de los usuarios de manera más efectiva, asegurando que cada usuario sea redirigido a la sección adecuada de la aplicación según su rol. Además, la funcionalidad de registro permite la creación de cuentas directamente desde la aplicación.

body:
This PR integrates the MinimaxSearch module with the GameManager's `analyze_layout` function to provide intelligent move recommendations based on search evaluation.

## Changes Made

### Core Integration
- **Modified `analyze_layout()` in `game.py`**: Now uses MinimaxSearch instead of simply listing legal moves
- **Added configurable search depth**: New constant `DEFAULT_SEARCH_DEPTH = 5` in `constants.py`
- **Smart recommendation display**: Shows format `"Recommended: XH -> R2C5 (score: 85.3)"` as specified

### Technical Implementation
```python
# Before: Simple move listing
for i, (card, (target_row, target_col)) in enumerate(legal_moves[:5]):
    card_str = f"{constants.RANK_MAP[card.rank]}{constants.SUIT_MAP[card.suit]}"
    print(f"  {card_str} -> R{target_row+1}C{target_col+1}")

# After: Search-based recommendations
search = MinimaxSearch(enable_diagnostics=True)
best_move = search.search(game_state, constants.DEFAULT_SEARCH_DEPTH)
# ... evaluation and formatted display
```

### Enhanced Features
- **Performance metrics**: Displays "Search evaluated X positions in Y seconds"
- **Error handling**: Graceful fallback when search fails
- **Backward compatibility**: All existing functionality preserved (legal moves list, reshuffle logic, diagnostics)

### Example Output
```
Analysis complete. Found 2 legal moves:
  Recommended: 2S -> R2C1 (score: 10.6)
  Search evaluated 2 positions in 0.000s
  Other legal moves:
    2S -> R2C1
    2S -> R4C1
```

## Testing
- ✅ All existing tests pass (search: 7/7, move executor: 6/6, evaluator: 6/6)
- ✅ Integration testing with live board scenarios
- ✅ Edge case handling (no moves, search errors)
- ✅ Output format verification matches requirements exactly

## Requirements Fulfilled
- ✅ Uses MinimaxSearch for recommendations with configurable depth
- ✅ Displays evaluation scores in the specified format
- ✅ Search depth configurable via constants
- ✅ Existing functionality remains intact

Fixes #23.

```
# Description

This PR introduces a new Large Language Model (LLM) provider, `BurncloudLLMClient`, integrating with the Burncloud API (`https://ai.burncloud.com/v1`).

This change expands the range of supported LLM services within the project, enabling access to various models including:
*   **Claude**: `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, `claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219`, `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022`
*   **GPT**: `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `o1`, `o1-mini`, `o1-preview`, `gpt-4-turbo`, `gpt-4-turbo-preview`, `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, `gpt-image-1`
*   **Gemini**: `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06`
*   **DeepSeek**: `deepseek-r1`, `deepseek-v3`

The implementation follows the existing `ProxyLLMClient` pattern, supporting both streaming and non-streaming generations, function calling, and automatic context length management.

**Dependencies:**
*   `openai` Python package.

# How Has This Been Tested?

A simple test was performed during development to verify the basic functionality of the `BurncloudLLMClient`. Code style and linting were checked using `ruff`.

**To reproduce:**
1.  Ensure the `openai` package is installed (`pip install openai`).
2.  Set your Burncloud API key as an environment variable:
    ```bash
    export BURNCLOUD_API_KEY="your_api_key_here"
    ```
3.  Optionally, set the API base if different from default:
    ```bash
    export BURNCLOUD_API_BASE="https://ai.burncloud.com/v1"
    ```
4.  Use the client in your code:
    ```python
    from dbgpt.core import ModelRequest, HumanMessage
    from dbgpt.model.proxy.llms.burncloud import BurncloudLLMClient
    import asyncio

    async def test_burncloud():
        client = BurncloudLLMClient()
        request = ModelRequest(model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022", messages=[HumanMessage(content="Hello, how are you today?")])
        
        print("--- Non-streaming test ---")
        output = await client.generate(request)
        print(f"Response: {output.text}")
        print(f"Usage: {output.usage}")

        print("\n--- Streaming test ---")
        async for chunk in client.generate_stream(request):
            print(chunk.text, end="", flush=True)
        print("\nStreaming complete.")

    if __name__ == "__main__":
        asyncio.run(test_burncloud())
    ```

author: ryanbreen
body:
## Summary

This PR contains a **critical fix** that enables direct userspace execution by solving the kernel stack mapping issue that was causing double faults during syscalls from Ring 3.

### 🎯 What Works Now

- ✅ **Direct userspace execution from kernel** - Kernel can create and run Ring 3 processes
- ✅ **Syscalls from userspace** - Ring 3 processes can successfully call `int 0x80`
- ✅ **"Hello from userspace\!" output** - Userspace programs can write to console via syscalls

### ❌ What Does NOT Work Yet

- ❌ **Fork syscall from userspace** - Not yet tested/validated
- ❌ **Exec syscall from userspace** - Not yet tested/validated  
- ❌ **Complete fork/exec pattern from Ring 3** - This is our NEXT goal

### 🔧 The Critical Fix

**Problem**: Double fault at `int 0x80` instruction (0x10000019) when userspace tried to make syscalls

**Root Cause**: 
- TSS RSP0 pointed to kernel stack at `0xffffc90000005000`
- This kernel stack was mapped in kernel page table
- But NOT mapped in userspace process page tables
- Ring 3 → Ring 0 transition failed accessing unmapped kernel stack

**Solution**: 
- Added `copy_kernel_stack_to_process()` function
- Maps kernel stack pages into process page tables during process creation
- Allows CPU to access kernel stack during privilege transitions

### 📁 Key Changes

1. **kernel/src/memory/process_memory.rs**
   - Added `copy_kernel_stack_to_process()` function (lines 307-360)
   - Maps kernel stack from kernel page table to process page table

2. **kernel/src/process/manager.rs**
   - Fixed direct process creation (lines 131-145)
   - Fixed fork process creation (lines 437-457)
   - Both paths now map kernel stack into process page tables

3. **docs/planning/06-userspace-execution/DIRECT_EXECUTION_FIX.md**
   - Complete technical documentation of the issue and fix
   - Mandatory regression testing requirements

### ✅ Evidence of Success

```
🎉 USERSPACE SYSCALL: Received INT 0x80 from userspace\!
✅ SUCCESS: Userspace syscall completed - wrote 49 bytes
Hello from userspace\! (via Rust syscall handler)
```

### 🚨 Mandatory Regression Testing

The direct execution test (`test_direct_execution()`) MUST pass on every kernel boot:
- Located in `kernel/src/test_exec.rs`
- Validates core syscall functionality
- Any failure indicates critical regression
- DO NOT proceed with fork/exec work until this passes consistently

### 📋 Next Steps

Now that direct execution works, we can proceed to:
1. Validate fork() syscall from userspace
2. Validate exec() syscall from userspace
3. Implement complete fork/exec pattern from Ring 3

This fix establishes the **foundation** - all future userspace work depends on this kernel stack mapping being correct.

## Problem The application was structured as a monolithic 879-line `App.tsx` component, which caused several issues: - Large bundle size with no code splitting - Poor performance on initial load - Difficult to maintain and debug - No component isolation for better caching ## Solution Refactored the monolithic component into a modular architecture with lazy-loaded components: ### Key Changes 1. **Created component structure** in `src/components/`: - `AboutSection.jsx` - Process steps and "Why Choose Us" section - `ServicesSection.jsx` - Service offerings and features - `PortfolioSection.jsx` - Project showcase - `ProcessSection.jsx` - Three-step process workflow - `ContactSection.jsx` - Contact form with state management 2. **Implemented React lazy loading**: ```javascript // Before: Everything in one file function App() { // 879 lines of code... } // After: Clean lazy-loaded components const AboutSection = lazy(() => import('./components/AboutSection.jsx')); const ServicesSection = lazy(() => import('./components/ServicesSection.jsx')); // ... other components return (
Loading Services...
}> {/* ... other lazy-loaded sections */} ); ``` 3. **Added Suspense wrappers** with loading states for better UX during component loading ### Performance Improvements **Bundle Analysis (before → after):** - Main bundle: 879 lines → ~300 lines - Code splitting: Monolithic → 5 separate chunks (1.32KB - 3.34KB each) - Lazy loading: All components load upfront → Components load on-demand - Caching: Single large bundle → Individual component caching **Build Output:** ``` dist/assets/ProcessSection-Bi-gTJjZ.js 1.32 kB │ gzip: 0.70 kB dist/assets/ContactSection-BYnJ1epO.js 2.42 kB │ gzip: 0.79 kB dist/assets/AboutSection-UviLGWUZ.js 2.62 kB │ gzip: 1.05 kB dist/assets/ServicesSection-B7dXqvj-.js 3.12 kB │ gzip: 1.29 kB dist/assets/PortfolioSection-CZUATpP5.js 3.34 kB │ gzip: 1.38 kB ``` ### Technical Details - **Browser Compatibility**: Used `.jsx` extensions for native ES module support - **State Management**: Preserved all existing functionality including form state in ContactSection - **Zero Breaking Changes**: Application works identically but with better performance - **Loading States**: Added proper loading fallbacks during component lazy loading ### Testing ✅ All components load correctly with lazy loading states ✅ Contact form functionality preserved and tested ✅ Build process generates proper code splitting ✅ No regression in existing functionality ✅ Performance improvements verified through bundle analysis ## Screenshot ![Working Application with Lazy Loading](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b06bd68-5846-440a-aa71-9abda694f06a) The application now loads efficiently with components being fetched only when needed, significantly improving initial load time and enabling better caching strategies. --- 💡 You can make Copilot smarter by setting up custom instructions, customizing its development environment and configuring Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. This pull request introduces several important updates to the project, primarily focused on replacing GORM with SQLC for ORM operations, modernizing database migration workflows, and improving developer tooling and CI processes. The changes also clean up legacy code, update documentation, and enhance configuration and testing practices.

**Migration from GORM to SQLC and related documentation updates:**

* Updated documentation in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `README.md` to reflect the replacement of GORM with SQLC as the project's ORM, including changes to recommended patterns for soft deletes and repository implementations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-227c2c26cb2ee0ce0f46a320fc48fbcbdf21801a57f59161b1d0861e8aad55f5L4-R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-227c2c26cb2ee0ce0f46a320fc48fbcbdf21801a57f59161b1d0861e8aad55f5L38-R38) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-227c2c26cb2ee0ce0f46a320fc48fbcbdf21801a57f59161b1d0861e8aad55f5L69-R71) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L12-R23)
* Added notes and checklists in `README.md` for SQLC implementation, migration workflow changes, and plans for further refactoring and testing improvements. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L12-R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R42-R55)

**Modernization of database migration workflow:**

* Removed legacy migration code (`cmd/migrate/main.go`) and updated the migration process to use the `golang-migrate` CLI via Makefile targets, including improved error handling and parameterization for migration commands. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-918e5643cec8e9b3393f6301dab40d8e7838fa28b72067549ebbbda244cecd75L1-L54) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52R17-R100)
* Updated CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`) to use new Makefile commands for migrations and testing, streamlining integration and coverage test execution.

**Tooling, configuration, and CI improvements:**

* Upgraded Go version to 1.25.1 across CI, Dockerfiles, and local development for consistency. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-944291df2c9c06359d37cc8833d182d705c9e8c3108e7cfe132d61a06e9133ddL9-R9) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557L1-R1) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-86930c95a19b82f7e64a962a0053d44e855824813019b3698eae4917a90cdcacL1-R1)
* Added `.mockery.yaml` configuration for generating mocks with testify, and refactored Makefile to automate mock and SQLC code generation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-531f7a01bb4f278f511fe2ada0896cfbbcb0771b7e53093d3a90c425882e4994R1-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52R109-L129)

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fe44f09c4d5977b5f5eaea29170b6a0748819c9d02271746a20d81a5f3efca17L5-L8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fe44f09c4d5977b5f5eaea29170b6a0748819c9d02271746a20d81a5f3efca17L47-R46) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-fe44f09c4d5977b5f5eaea29170b6a0748819c9d02271746a20d81a5f3efca17L72-L108)
